tasks.title: Fix missing RESIDENT value in Postgres userrole enum
tasks.justification: URGENT hotfix, independently verified against a real Postgres instance (postgres:16-alpine in Docker), not just SQLite. Added Alembic migration 0014_add_resident_userrole (chained after 0013_add_construction_project, same ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS idiom as 0003_add_guest_to_userrole_enum.py). Verified end-to-end in Docker: fresh-database upgrade to head applies cleanly, a real INSERT with role='RESIDENT' succeeds via raw SQL, alembic downgrade -1 is a safe no-op (Postgres cannot drop enum values, matching 0003's precedent, then upgrade head re-applies idempotently). Added backend/tests/test_migrations_postgres.py: 3 tests that run Alembic via subprocess against a real Postgres reachable via TEST_POSTGRES_URL (enum contains RESIDENT, INSERT with role=RESIDENT succeeds, downgrade no-op) -- skipped (not failed) when TEST_POSTGRES_URL is unset since CI has no Postgres service, documenting the known SQLite-can't-verify-Postgres-enum-constraints gap. Full backend suite: 287 passed, 3 skipped (the new Postgres-only tests, by design), 96.22% coverage (>90% gate), no regressions. Grepped for other hardcoded 4-value role lists (document.py/schemas/document.py allowed_roles defaults, 0001_initial_schema.py's literal sa.Enum(...) column, RBAC role-set checks) -- none needed changes, all already correct or intentionally excluding RESIDENT for admin-only gates. Scope strictly limited to the database enum fix, no resident UI/business logic added.
expected_results: Alembic migration adds RESIDENT to the Postgres userrole enum type (same idiom as migration 0003_add_guest_to_userrole_enum.py)
A test verifies the enum accepts RESIDENT against a real Postgres instance (not just SQLite)
Migration runs cleanly upgrade+downgrade against a real Postgres instance
